messages:
mira: Quick Q — where can I find per-dedicated-pool autoscale graphs + which signals we treat as 'saturation' vs noise? Trying to tune alerts for ded-east-idx, we've been getting a lot of flaps this week.

sam: Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/0a1b2c/pool-inspector?var-pool=ded-east-idx — check these panels: active_workers, pending_queue, alloc_rate, latency_p50_p95, kv_cache_hit. For saturation look for sustained pending_queue + rising p95. Also there's a derived metric rw.pool.saturation_score.

anya: Two heuristics we've had success with: 1) sustained pending_queue > 50 for 5m (this usually means real capacity pressure). 2) p95 latency > 300ms AND pending trending up. Use a "for: 10m" window on monitors to avoid paging on single spikes.

lee: Logs/traces: Loki query: {pool="ded-east-idx"} |= "backpressure" or |= "throttle". Traces/Jaeger: filter service=runtime + tag pool=ded-east-idx. Example jaeger search link: https://jaeger.redwood.internal/search?service=runtime&tag=pool:ded-east-idx

sam: Example Datadog monitor we use as a starting point:
```
avg(last_5m):max:rw.pool.pending_queue{pool:ded-east-idx} > 50
```
Add a companion monitor for p95: `avg(last_5m):max:rw.request.latency_p95{pool:ded-east-idx} > 0.3` with a 10m notify window.

mira: Nice. Any guidance on priority/owners? Ops has been getting paged on p95 spikes that resolve quickly.

anya: Recommendation: P0 only for sustained saturation (pending + p95 for >10m). P1 for transient p95 spikes. Owner should be the oncall for pool-eng (add runbook link). Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/pool-saturation

ops-bot: deploy-bot: FYI next autoscaler rollout scheduled 2026-03-18 02:00 UTC — expect transient rebalancing, may trigger short-lived alerts :information_source:

lee: One more: use `rw.pool.saturation_score` (weighted function of pending, p95, worker_util). Threshold we've been using as guardrail is >0.7. It reduces noise compared to single-metric triggers.

mira: Perfect — I'll update the monitor and open a PR. @sam can you do a quick review when I post? :pray:
